shewhart_individuals_and_gx.timing_discrepancy_summary: First alarm state occurs on day of onset (lag 0) because the process was already in an active alarm excursion (Episode 15) that began on 2012-06-13 (18 days before onset). The first genuine new post-onset threshold crossing does not occur until 2012-10-31 (lag 122 days).

tabular_cusum.timing_discrepancy_summary: CUSUM accumulator (C+) crossed h=5.0 on 2012-03-07 and remained continuously above 5.0 for 300 days through 2012-12-31 under reset_policy='none'. Thus, zero new post-onset threshold crossings occurred. The reported 100% batch recall is an artifact of pre-existing seasonal saturation, not sensitivity to the shift.

gx_and_p_chart.timing_consistency_summary: Zero pre-onset false alarms. The first alarm state coincides exactly with the first new threshold crossing on 2012-06-10, demonstrating clean event detection with 0 lag relative to realized defect injection.

discrepancies_flagged.reported_text: On 2012-07-01, Shewhart was on day 4 of an ongoing summer excursion that began on 2012-06-28.
discrepancies_flagged.verified_fact: Shewhart Episode 15 actually began on 2012-06-13 (when cnt_mean crossed UCL=208.68 to reach 309.21), not 2012-06-28. June 13 to June 30 is 18 days; on 2012-07-01, Shewhart was on day 19 of the excursion. This was a narrative counting error in the preliminary audit note. All generated publication CSV tables (table_alarm_episodes.csv, comparative_metrics.csv) and daily alert series correctly record Episode 15 beginning on 2012-06-13.
